brief: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping the CFO title. The stock fell as much as 13% intraday, closing down about 4%; CoreWeave fell 11% the same day while marketing a $4bn+ loan Nvidia likely guarantees. The piece catalogs Nvidia's circular AI financing web: $99bn of equity stakes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Safe Superintelligence, xAI/SpaceX, neoclouds, suppliers, Hugging Face), $108.5bn of guarantees (including a $105bn OpenAI Ohio backstop that Kress, not Huang, halved), and $366bn of future commitments, totaling $530.5bn excluding Huang's pledge to backstop up to $125bn (25%) of a separate $500bn financing platform that has produced no deals in three months. Per WSJ reporting, Huang's son-in-law Nico Caprez had been running aggressive financing deals; Kress pushed back, was dismissed by Huang as 'a deer in the headlights,' then curbed the program from August. Goldman, UBS and William Blair all flag that new financing deals, not existing ones, get harder without Huang, raising competitive risk from Broadcom and AMD. Nvidia reports Q3 earnings Tuesday Nov 17, the first test of whether the financing machine still runs.
